SRC-254:R001.text: Do not assume which cause applies without evidence.

SRC-254:R002.text: An otherwise functional Windows SAIPEN installation must not unnecessarily depend on one hardcoded Git Bash path.

SRC-254:R003.text: Do not weaken security or bypass the host's execution boundaries.

SRC-254:R004.text: Do not conflate host process-spawn failure with SAIPEN lifecycle refusal.

SRC-254:R005.text: Do not introduce another competing runtime manager.

SRC-254:R006.text: Do not require Git Bash merely to execute a Python-based SAIPEN continuation if an existing supported native launcher provides equivalent behavior.

SRC-254:R007.text: Do not translate arbitrary POSIX commands into PowerShell without proving behavioral equivalence.

SRC-254:R008.text: Do not patch Freebuff source from SAIPEN authority.

SRC-254:R009.text: Avoid adding SAIPEN compatibility layers that cannot repair a failure occurring before the SAIPEN process starts.

SRC-254:R010.text: Do not repeatedly execute the same command when its executable is known to be missing.

SRC-254:R011.text: Do not treat installation of Git Bash as the only possible recovery.

SRC-254:R012.text: Do not silently install software, modify system PATH, or elevate privileges without the required authorization.

SRC-254:R013.text: Its actual project root and live authority must be established independently.

SRC-254:R014.text: Do not claim T-52 is repaired.

SRC-254:R015.text: Do not modify its project source from SAIPEN authority.

SRC-254:R016.text: The final host acceptance must distinguish:

SRC-254:R017.text: Do not promote unit-test success to real host acceptance.

SRC-254:R019.text: A missing shell executable must not become a week-long protocol recovery incident.

SRC-254:R020.text: The responsible host or runtime component must provide a deterministic execution route or an accurate actionable refusal.

SRC-254:R021.text: Determine the exact failure owner from SAIPEN bootstrap, activation, machine/runtime entry contracts and actual Freebuff spawn evidence; classify A-G without treating host spawn failure as lifecycle refusal.

SRC-254:R022.text: Reuse a trusted existing native Windows launcher only through an execution route the host supports and authorizes; preserve runtime generation, original project binding and provenance.

SRC-254:R023.text: If Freebuff owns the failure, provide a precise independently admitted handoff with affected component, configured path, verified alternatives, required fixes, negative controls and cold-start acceptance; do not patch its source here.

SRC-254:R024.text: Record controlled Windows cases A-E for Bash present, unavailable configured Bash with native launcher, Bash-only host, missing/untrusted machine runtime, and absent lifecycle authority; distinguish harness evidence from running-host evidence.

SRC-254:R025.text: Real Freebuff Desktop GPT-6 Luna cold-start with exact input cc must route to SAIPEN without repeated missing-shell attempts or conflicting SAIPAL activation and reach genuine Work or authoritative refusal.

SRC-254:R026.text: Independently establish T-52 project identity, current STATE, owner, admission, source and applicability; preserve original Work and resume only under target-project authorization, otherwise state the exact blocker.

SRC-254:R027.text: For a recoverable failure identify executable or CWD/configuration, verify an authorized trusted route, preserve original task and project, resume idempotently and report the actual result; no unchanged retry loop.

SRC-254:R028.text: Report SOURCE_VERIFIED, WINDOWS_RUNTIME_VERIFIED, FREEBUFF_HOST_VERIFIED, REAL_LUNA_ACCEPTANCE and BLOCKED separately, with actual counts and exact next host-owned or canonical action.

SRC-254:R029.text: Finish currently admitted work before changing source, admit any SAIPEN implementation canonically, and add no runtime manager, persistent registry, authority source, shell framework or mandatory operator steps.
